rootCauseAnalysis.description: The search results row locator waits only 3 seconds for SAP Fiori's search autocomplete to populate results. On the first attempt, SAP's backend response took longer than 3s, causing timeout. On retry (with warmed network/cache), results loaded faster and the test passed.
rootCauseAnalysis.evidenceFromRetry: Retry #1 passed successfully with identical locator strategy, proving SAP app behavior is correct but timing is inconsistent.

issues.description: WAITS.SEARCH_RESULTS = 3000ms is too aggressive for SAP Fiori search autocomplete under variable network conditions
Line 192 uses waitForTimeout(WAITS.SEARCH_RESULTS) — fixed 3s wait instead of dynamic wait for search results container to appear

strengths: Role-based locator is semantically correct for SAP Fiori table rows

rationale: Test passed on retry with identical code, proving SAP app works correctly. Failure is purely due to insufficient timeout for search results to appear. This is a classic flaky test pattern caused by overly aggressive timing constraints.

recommendedFixes.change: Increase WAITS.SEARCH_RESULTS from 3000ms to 10000ms (10 seconds) to accommodate SAP Fiori search backend latency
Replace `await this.page.waitForTimeout(WAITS.SEARCH_RESULTS)` with dynamic wait for search results dropdown/container to appear (e.g., waitForSelector on search results list)
Wrap resultRow.waitFor() in a retry loop (2-3 attempts) to handle transient SAP search delays

explorationComparison.note: Exploration data not consulted for this analysis because retry succeeded with identical code, proving locator strategy is correct. Issue is timing only.

notes: This is a textbook flaky test caused by insufficient timeout. The locator strategy itself is correct (proven by retry success). SAP Fiori search autocomplete has variable backend response time. Fix: increase timeout from 3s to 10s.
nextStep: Apply timeout increase to WAITS.SEARCH_RESULTS in purchase-order.locators.js and re-run test to verify stability
